unit.why: A brief anecdote (a prayer leader displeases R. Naftali of Ropshitz during his stay in Zhidachov, and R. Zvi Hirsh answers with a teaching) is followed by separate sayings of R. Zvi Hirsh without narrative.
unit.boundary_note: the anecdote is followed in the same division by unrelated sayings (yihud before eating; the Besht's sixty disciples); the next division begins another teaching

stories.start_quote: בהיות הה״ק מהר״נ מראפשיטץ ז״ל בזידיטשוב
stories.end_quote: כי הבעל תפלה הוא טפל להצדיק
stories.summary_en: While R. Naftali of Ropshitz was in Zhidachov, a man who led the prayers displeased him. R. Zvi Hirsh answered with the Maggid of Kozhenitz's reading of the Talmud's story of the High Priest, Shemaya and Avtalyon: the tzaddikim give the prayer leader his power, so the prayer leader is secondary to the tzaddik.
